content:
Solve \( \cos 2x = \sin x \):
\[
1-2\sin^2 x = \sin x \implies 2\sin^2 x+\sin x-1=0
\]
\[
(2\sin x-1)(\sin x+1)=0
\]
So \(\sin x=\frac12\) or \(\sin x=-1\).

Evaluate \(y=\sin 2x+2\cos x-3\):

- If \(\sin x=-1\), then \(\cos x=0\), so \(y=-3\).
- If \(\sin x=\frac12\), then \(\cos x=\pm \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\). Also \(\sin 2x=2\sin x\cos x=\cos x\), so
\[
y=3\cos x-3.
\]
This is largest when \(\cos x=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\), giving
\[
y=3\cdot \frac{\sqrt3}{2}-3=\frac{3\sqrt3-6}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{3\sqrt3-6}{2}}
\]
